title: Error when loading custom resource through `load()`
body:
### Tested versions

- 4.4.stable.mono
- 4.4.1.stable.mono
- 4.5.beta6

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon R5 Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.20913.2000) - AMD A6-7480 Radeon R5, 8 Compute Cores 2C+6G (2 threads)

### Issue description

While working on my RTS game, all of a sudden I started getting an error at runtime
```
E 0:00:03:988   RTSGameWorld._enter_tree: Trying to assign value of type 'Resource' to a variable of type 'ref_class_obj.gd'.
  <GDScript Source>game_world.gd:20 @ RTSGameWorld._enter_tree()
  <Stack Trace> game_world.gd:20 @ _enter_tree()
```
Even though the code that's causing it has been there for some time now, and only recently did the error start happening
```gdscript
func _enter_tree() -> void:
	var object_ref_dir: String = "res://data/objects/refs/"
	for file in ResourceLoader.list_directory(object_ref_dir):
		var ref: RTSObjectRef = load(object_ref_dir + file) # This is line 20, the one the error happens on
		object_scenes[ref] = load(ref.object_scene)
		if not ref.object_model_scene.is_empty():
			object_models[ref] = load(ref.object_model_scene)
		object_infos[ref] = load(ref.object_info)
	var upgrade_ref_dir: String = "res://data/upgrades/refs/"
	for file in ResourceLoader.list_directory(upgrade_ref_dir):
		var ref: RTSUpgradeRef = load(upgrade_ref_dir + file)
		upgrade_scenes[ref] = load(ref.upgrade_scene)
```
Here's the `RTSObjectRef` class script:
```gdscript
extends RTSBaseRef
class_name RTSObjectRef

@export_file("*.tscn") var object_scene: String
@export_file("*.tscn") var object_model_scene: String
@export_file("*.tres") var object_info: String
```
And its parent class, `RTSBaseRef`:
```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name RTSBaseRef
## Base class for [RTSObjectRef] and [RTSUpgradeRef].

func _to_string() -> String:
	return get_ref_name()

## Returns the resource's filename (without the extension).
func get_ref_name() -> String:
	return (resource_path.get_file().get_slice(".", 0))
```

**Addendum 26/08:** I've found that in actuality, the first resource file in the folder successfully loads, and when the for-loop runs again for the next file, *then* the error happens
Also, the debugger shows that file from the previous for-loop that successfully loaded as the value of `ref` in the failed loop. Don't know whether that means something or it's just a harmless quirk of the editor

### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like this can be reproduced in isolation. I tried with an MRP but the code works just fine there, both on 4.4.1 and 4.5.beta6

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[CustomResourceMRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21975031/CustomResourceMRP.zip)
